outcome: No proof or disproof of the infinitude of regular primes, and no progress on the conjectured e^{-1/2} density, has appeared since 26 January 2024; the problem remains exactly as open as Wikipedia's frozen statement describes.
summary: This is an infinitude/density existence question, so under §3.1 it moves only when actually answered — extending a computational record does not count. I searched broadly for any 2024-2026 proof, disproof, or substantive progress on (a) whether infinitely many regular primes exist, and (b) whether their density is e^{-1/2}, and found nothing. The current Wikipedia 'Regular prime' article (fetched live) confirms the infinitude question is still described as unsolved, states the same e^{-1/2}≈60.65% Siegel conjecture, and its most recent computational record is still Hart, Harvey and Ong's 2016/2017 'Irregular primes to two billion' (arXiv:1605.02398, published in Math. Comp. 86 (2017)) — no newer extension of that table was found, and even if one existed it would not change the status per §3.1 since a search bound is not an answer to an infinitude question. I also checked adjacent literature that surfaces under 'regular primes' searches — a 2023 Lean formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes (arXiv:2305.08955, formalized further in arXiv:2410.01466) and a 2023 paper on regular primes/non-Wieferich primes/multiple zeta values (arXiv:2310.06809) — both are about consequences of or related structures to regular primes (FLT for regular exponents; connections to Wieferich primes and MZVs), not about the stated question of infinitude or density, so they are out of scope under the case-vs-variant test in §3.1 and do not change anything here. I found no AI system anywhere near this problem: searches for AI/ML work on regular primes turned up only tangential hits (a formal-impossibility result about ML and prime-generating formulas, an unrelated AI-verified Lean proof of the bounded-prime-gaps theorem, and AI-and-Goldbach's-conjecture experiments), none of which bear on regular primes' infinitude or density. I agree with the triage verdict of 'none' and reached the same conclusion independently.
competing_reading: None. The line between 'case of the problem' and 'related problem' is not in play here since nothing relevant was found at all; the only judgment call was whether the irregular-prime search-record extensions (which don't exist post-2024 anyway) would count, and per the existence/infinitude rule in §3.1 they would not even if found.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof that there are infinitely many regular primes (settling the first half), or a proof of the conjectured e^{-1/2} density (settling the second half, contingent on infinitude). Absent either, the entry stays open exactly as Wikipedia states it.
